books.title: Crooked Kingdom
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
books.blurb: Kaz Brekker and his crew pulled off the impossible and got nothing for it. Back in Ketterdam, double-crossed and badly out of pocket, they are hunted by rival gangs, a merchant council that wants them buried, and a foreign government that wants one of them back. With a member of the crew in enemy hands, Kaz has to out-scheme an entire city — and this time the con is personal. The second half of the Six of Crows duology.

books.title: Six of Crows
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
books.blurb: Ketterdam is a city that runs on debt, and Kaz Brekker collects. Offered a fortune he cannot turn down, he assembles six dangerous outcasts — a sharpshooter, a runaway, a spy, a Heartrender, a thief and a convict — to break into the Ice Court, the most secure fortress in the world, and pull out the scientist who invented a drug that turns Grisha power into a weapon. Six narrators, six agendas, and no honest people anywhere.

review.text: Thrilling and Captivating. Did not see anything comming

books.title: Bridge to Terabithia
books.author: Katherine Paterson
books.blurb: The story tells about the blooming friendship between two kids, Jesse Aarons, and his new neighbour, Leslie Burke, two lonely kids.

recs.title: The Book Thief
recs.author: Markus Zusak
recs.blurb: Narrated by Death himself, this is the story of Liesel Meminger, a foster girl in Nazi Germany who steals books she cannot yet read and reads them aloud in bomb shelters. When her family hides a Jewish man in their basement, words become the most dangerous and most saving thing she owns.

recs.author: George Orwell
recs.blurb: Winston Smith rewrites history for a living in a state where the Party controls the past, the present and the language itself. His quiet rebellion — a diary, a love affair, a rented room — runs headlong into a machine built to make rebellion unthinkable.

recs.title: The Kite Runner
recs.author: Khaled Hosseini
recs.blurb: Amir and Hassan are inseparable in 1970s Kabul until one winter afternoon at a kite tournament, when Amir's silence costs Hassan everything. Decades later, safe in California, an old phone call gives him one chance to go back. Spans the Soviet invasion and the rise of the Taliban, but stays a story about cowardice and what it takes to undo it.

recs.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
recs.author: Harper Lee
recs.blurb: Scout Finch grows up in Depression-era Alabama watching her father defend a Black man falsely accused of assault. A courtroom drama told from a child's shoulder height, where the neighbour everyone fears turns out to be the one paying attention.

recs.title: The Elevator Ghost
recs.author: Glen Huser
recs.blurb: Carolina Giddle arrives at the Blatchford Arms in sequinned sneakers with a tarantula named Chiquita and a talent for babysitting the building's most impossible children. Her method is simple: tell each one a ghost story built exactly to their size. Six linked tales — creepy, funny, and just scary enough — leading to a Halloween party and a very suspicious departure.

recs.title: Heart of a Champion
recs.author: Ellen Schwartz
recs.blurb: Kenny Sakamoto worships his older brother Mickey and the Vancouver Asahi baseball team, and wants nothing more than a place on the field. Then Pearl Harbor is bombed and his Japanese-Canadian community is uprooted to the interior. A coming-of-age story about a boy holding on to the one thing that still makes sense.

recs.title: Finding Grace
recs.author: Becky Citra
recs.blurb: It's 1954, and eleven-year-old Hope has spent years writing letters to a sister she believes she invented. When she discovers Grace is real — a twin given up for adoption after contracting polio — Hope sets out to find her, and to reach the mother who has gone quiet in the next room.

recs.title: Look Out for the Fitzgerald-Trouts
recs.author: Esta Spalding
recs.blurb: Four loosely related children live in a car on a tropical island. They bathe in the ocean, fish for dinner, pick fruit for breakfast, and drive themselves to school — all while hunting for a real home. Witty, warm, and quietly serious about what family means when the adults have opted out.

recs.title: Pandas on the Eastside
recs.author: Gabrielle Prendergast
recs.blurb: Vancouver, 1970s. Ten-year-old Journey Song finds two pandas stranded in a warehouse in her neighbourhood, caught up in a diplomatic standoff and going quietly neglected. She has no money and no connections, so she uses what her block does have: everybody on it.

recs.title: Heartless
recs.author: Marissa Meyer
recs.blurb: Before she was the Queen of Hearts, Catherine wanted to open a bakery. The King of Hearts wants to marry her; her parents want the match; and Jest, the new court joker, wants something he won't name. A Wonderland origin story that starts as a confection and ends somewhere much colder.

recs.title: The Cruel Prince
recs.author: Holly Black
recs.blurb: Jude and her two sisters are taken to the High Court of Faerie as children, after the fae knight Madoc kills their parents and claims them as his own. Ten years on, Jude is seventeen and mortal in a world that treats humans as pets or amusements, and she wants a place at court badly enough to bleed for it. Standing in her way is Prince Cardan, the youngest son of the High King, who makes her humiliation something close to a hobby. The court runs on old rules about lying, debts, and hospitality, and Jude learns quickly that the rules are the only weapon a human gets.

recs.title: The Namesake
recs.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
recs.blurb: Ashoke and Ashima Ganguli leave Calcutta for a university town outside Boston, where they raise two children in a country whose customs never quite become their own. Their son carries the name Gogol, chosen under hospital pressure and tied to something in his father's past, and he spends much of his life resenting it. The novel follows the family across decades, moving between the parents' careful preservation of what they left behind and the children's easy, sometimes careless American lives. Lahiri writes in a quiet register, attentive to meals, houses, and the small negotiations that make up a marriage.
